sections.skill: Compare monthly payments and total interest for different mortgage terms and rates

questions.prompt: A $240,000 mortgage at 6.5% for 30 years has a principal-and-interest payment of $1,516.96. What is the total of all 360 payments?
questions.intro: Total paid on a mortgage = monthly payment × number of payments. Total interest = total paid − amount borrowed. On long loans, interest can exceed the original loan.
sources: CFPB (Interest rate vs. APR): The interest rate is the cost of borrowing the principal; the APR also includes certain fees, so payment math uses the note interest rate, and APR equals that rate only when there are no other finance charges. (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/what-is-the-difference-between-a-loan-interest-rate-and-the-apr-en-733/)

questions.prompt: Why might a buyer choose the 30-year loan despite its higher total interest?

choices.text: It always has a lower interest rate than a 15-year loan
It is paid off sooner
Its lower monthly payment is easier to afford
It has lower total interest because payments are smaller

questions.correct_answer: Its lower monthly payment is easier to afford
questions.feedback: The 30-year loan trades higher total cost for a lower monthly payment.

misconceptions.D: Confuses payment size with total cost

questions.prompt: The payment formula is M = P · r ÷ (1 − (1 + r)^(−n)). For a 30-year loan with a 6.5% interest (note) rate, what are r and n?
questions.intro: Monthly mortgage payments use the same formula as other installment loans, with the monthly rate r = annual note (interest) rate ÷ 12 and n = number of monthly payments. A mortgage APR also includes fees, so it is not the rate used in this formula.
questions.feedback: Monthly rate = annual interest rate ÷ 12; 30 years = 360 months.
sources: CFPB (Interest rate vs. APR): The interest rate is the cost of borrowing the principal; the APR also includes certain fees, so payment math uses the note interest rate, and APR equals that rate only when there are no other finance charges. (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/what-is-the-difference-between-a-loan-interest-rate-and-the-apr-en-733/)

questions.prompt: Using the formula, what is the monthly principal-and-interest payment on $240,000 at a 5.5% interest rate for 30 years (nearest cent)?
questions.intro: Evaluate the formula with a calculator: find r = annual interest rate ÷ 12 and n = 360, compute (1 + r)^(−n), then the payment.

It is more than the loan ÷ number of months

When rates are fixed

questions.prompt: Why compare Loan Estimates from several lenders on the same day?

choices.text: Rates change daily, so same-day quotes compare fairly
Lenders must match each other's rates by law each day
It locks the rate with every lender at once
Each extra quote lowers your score a lot

questions.correct_answer: Rates change daily, so same-day quotes compare fairly
questions.intro: Mortgage rates change frequently. Comparing standardized Loan Estimates gathered at the same time gives a fair comparison.
questions.feedback: Same-day Loan Estimates compare like with like.

misconceptions.D: Overstates the effect of rate shopping
